references.text: The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the veil of the sanctuary. The same ritual action of sprinkling seven times.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, in front of the veil. A parallel to the sprinkling seven times with the finger.
Moses sprinkled oil on the altar seven times to consecrate it. Sevenfold sprinkling for consecration.
He shall sprinkle seven times on the one being cleansed from leprosy. The same pattern of sevenfold sprinkling for cleansing.
Sprinkling of blood with the finger seven times on the mercy seat. The same context on the Day of Atonement with sevenfold sprinkling.
Atonement for the sanctuary because of the impurities of the people of Israel. The same theme of cleansing from the uncleanness of Israel.
The priest shall take some of the blood with his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting. Sprinkling with the finger seven times for cleansing.
Blood shall be sprinkled on the horns and corners of the altar to cleanse it and make atonement. Cleansing and consecration of the altar with blood.

Moses sprinkled blood on the tabernacle and all the vessels used in the service. Almost everything is cleansed by blood according to the law. The letter to the Hebrews explains the significance of blood sprinkling for cleansing.
